relevance_note: Case report of one woman with a GFAP variant: "a 25-year-old woman with genetically confirmed (p.R276L mutation in the GFAP gene) juvenile-onset AxD".
method_note: Read the whole paper; JSON built by a short Python script from hand-written values, every span checked verbatim by script. Scope: the patient; her mother (tested negative: 'The mutation was not found in her mother.') as a tested relative, with no variant row because she does not carry the variant. The father ('could not be investigated', parents described as 'healthy') was neither tested nor affected, so no row; inheritance therefore 'not reported' (only one parent tested). Previously published people: ref [10] patient included (one case, individual-level course: partial remission lasting less than 5 years). Not given rows: hereditary [4] and sporadic [5] cases with p.R276L (plural 'cases', number of people not stated); patients of refs [7, 8] (group statement 'the patients in the literature' about dysphagia and dysphonia, not attributable per person); the 20-year-old patient of ref [11] (no diagnosis of Alexander disease or GFAP variant stated for that patient). Age at onset recorded as onset of episodic vomiting at age nine (abstract 'Episodic vomiting appeared at age nine'); earlier febrile seizures at 1 year and small food intake from age three are recorded as features with their own onset. General negative statements recorded as written and not used to exclude more specific checklist items (D-27): 'no neurological deficits, except for episodic postprandial vomiting', 'Gastrointestinal, metabolic, endocrinological and psychological disorders were ruled out', 'No other signal abnormalities were noted', and 'Episodic vomiting, which was the only sign of bulbar dysfunction' (dysphagia and dysarthria/dysphonia left not reported). Narrow absences not used for broader checklist items: 'abnormalities in the basal ganglia' absent does not exclude 'basal ganglia or thalamic abnormality'; 'leukodystrophy in deep white matter' absent does not exclude 'cerebral white matter abnormality'; 'ventricular garlands' absent not used for 'periventricular rim'. Cognitive decline marked excluded from normal intelligence at age 11 and at age 25. Vital status 'alive' from present-tense description at age 25. Pathogenicity is the authors' statement that this mutation was previously described as responsible for adult-onset AxD; no ACMG class given. No contradictions found.
